ownership_reason: Only the gold decides the written form of each byte of the data, including the last one: it writes the quoted-printable form without soft line breaks, one unit per byte. Hops 1, 3 and 4 pass the data along; hop 2 only places soft line breaks over the gold's units (never after the last unit) and escapes a raw space or tab that one of its soft line breaks follows, copying every other unit as it is. The end of the gold's output is therefore the end of the last encoded line, and once the gold has written the last byte, a tab, as it is, the escape '=09' can appear only if a caller rewrites the gold's output or replaces the gold. The gold's javadoc promises the quoted-printable form, in which a line must not end in a space or tab (RFC 1521 rule #3, cited by the class javadoc); the variant ends the encoded text with a raw tab. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the intact sibling QuotedPrintableCodec.encodeQuotedPrintable(BitSet, byte[]) does the same step ('rule #3: trailing whitespace shall be encoded': a space or tab that is the last byte is escaped) and is used in production by QCodec.doEncoding and by QuotedPrintableCodec.encode(byte[]) and encode(String, String); testTrailingSpecial (through the chain: a tab followed by a soft line break is escaped) and testFinalBytes (through the chain: a space with no line end after it stays as it is) pass, as do testUTF8RoundTrip and testEncodeUrlWithNullBitSet on the sibling path.
